value.rationale: Two-contact excitation on a canonical width-two graph destroys persistent excitations despite graph length, with an exact and sharp five-update bound. The complete radius-three witness characterizes maximal extinction latency by a natural local causal event; the 204-state automaton counts all initial states with this event. A rigorous disjoint-block lower bound shows maximal latency becomes asymptotically typical, a nontrivial contrast of deterministic extinction and random-initial-state saturation. This goes beyond renaming a known table or a single unmotivated small graph.
